sentences.heading: Purpose
sentences.sentence: KF-SAS-RQ-001.** The Fabric SHALL present one coherent typed graph over records whose authorities remain distinct, and SHALL record for every record which authority owns it.

sentences.heading: Architectural thesis
sentences.sentence: KF-SAS-RQ-002.** Visibility, immutability and referential integrity SHALL be enforced in the database, and the application layer SHALL NOT be the sole enforcement point for any of them.

sentences.heading: Architectural thesis
sentences.sentence: KF-SAS-RQ-003.** An access context that has not been bound SHALL read nothing, and the default classification rank SHALL be below the lowest classification.

sentences.heading: Law 1 — One canonical authority per fact
sentences.sentence: KF-SAS-RQ-010.** Every record SHALL name its authority, and a mirrored record SHALL be distinguishable from an authoritative one by a recorded field, not by convention.

sentences.heading: Law 2 — Every controlled write is an attributed act
sentences.sentence: KF-SAS-RQ-011.** A controlled state change SHALL be recorded as an act naming its actor, acting role and targets, in the same transaction that applies it.

sentences.heading: Law 3 — A refusal is a feature
sentences.sentence: KF-SAS-RQ-012.** Every refusal the dispatcher makes SHALL carry one of the named failure codes and a detail object, and SHALL NOT surface as an untyped error.

sentences.heading: Law 4 — Fail closed
sentences.sentence: KF-SAS-RQ-013.** Where a check cannot be performed, the system SHALL refuse rather than proceed, and a gate that compared nothing SHALL NOT report success.

sentences.heading: Law 5 — Identity never changes meaning
sentences.sentence: KF-SAS-RQ-014.** An allocated identifier SHALL never be reissued or re-meant, and a retired namespace SHALL remain resolvable.

sentences.heading: Law 6 — Retire by sequester, never delete
sentences.sentence: KF-SAS-RQ-015.** Withdrawal, supersession, revocation and unpublication SHALL be recorded state changes, and SHALL NOT be implemented as deletion.

sentences.heading: Law 7 — Canonical before hashed
sentences.sentence: KF-SAS-RQ-016.** Every digest SHALL be computed over an RFC 8785 canonical form under a named format tag, and the tag SHALL be part of the preimage.

sentences.heading: Law 8 — Generated artifacts are never hand-edited
sentences.sentence: KF-SAS-RQ-017.** A generated artifact SHALL be reproducible from its source, and a difference between the committed artifact and a fresh build SHALL fail the build.

sentences.heading: Law 9 — Gaps are recorded, never marked
sentences.sentence: KF-SAS-RQ-018.** A known gap SHALL be recorded in an enumerable place, and SHALL NOT be recorded only as an inline source comment.

sentences.heading: Law 10 — Some acts are not the software's to perform
sentences.sentence: KF-SAS-RQ-019.** The acts listed in §22 SHALL be performable only by a human actor, and the system SHALL refuse them to a service actor by name.

sentences.heading: Non-goals
sentences.sentence: KF-SAS-RQ-190.** Business logic SHALL be computed by callers and SHALL reach the Fabric only as attributed acts through the dispatcher.

sentences.heading: Non-goals
sentences.sentence: KF-SAS-RQ-191.** If dataset, transform or lineage capability is built, it SHALL be a core primitive governed by the same act, audit, access and provenance model as every other record, and SHALL NOT reach storage outside that model.

sentences.heading: `OH-DOC-000002-1-R01` — the domain specification
sentences.sentence: KF-SAS-RQ-022.** The ontology SHALL preserve every approved R01 definition byte-identically, and SHALL declare every addition beyond R01 by name.

sentences.heading: Implementation basis
sentences.sentence: KF-SAS-RQ-023.** Exactly one package SHALL be permitted to open a database connection, and exactly one package SHALL provide the controlled write path.

sentences.heading: Conformance language
sentences.sentence: SHALL** states a requirement.

sentences.heading: Conformance language
sentences.sentence: SHALL NOT** states a prohibition.

sentences.heading: Conformance language
sentences.sentence: SHOULD** states a strong recommendation whose exceptions must be recorded.

sentences.heading: Conformance language
sentences.sentence: MAY** states an option.

sentences.heading: How to read the state claims in this document
sentences.sentence: SHALL** — this is a requirement of the architecture.

sentences.heading: Objects and identity
sentences.sentence: KF-SAS-RQ-030.** Every governed record SHALL have exactly one `core.object` row carrying its identity, type, lifecycle state, organization, classification and row version.

sentences.heading: Objects and identity
sentences.sentence: KF-SAS-RQ-031.** The time an event occurred and the time it was recorded SHALL be separately recorded, and the recorded time SHALL be assigned by the server.

sentences.heading: Enterprise identifiers
sentences.sentence: KF-SAS-RQ-032.** An enterprise identifier SHALL be opaque and SHALL carry a check character that detects single-character and adjacent-transposition errors.

sentences.heading: Enterprise identifiers
sentences.sentence: KF-SAS-RQ-033.** The request that allocates an identifier SHALL have no field in which a caller can name, suggest or influence the identifier allocated.

sentences.heading: Organizations, people and roles
sentences.sentence: KF-SAS-RQ-034.** Every act SHALL name an acting role assignment, and the system SHALL verify that assignment is live before applying any change.

sentences.heading: Organizations, people and roles
sentences.sentence: KF-SAS-RQ-035.** Only a human person SHALL carry an external authentication identity.

sentences.heading: Classification
sentences.sentence: KF-SAS-RQ-036.** Classification SHALL be a closed, totally ordered set, and comparison SHALL be by rank.

sentences.heading: Clearance and the effective ceiling
sentences.sentence: KF-SAS-RQ-037.** A caller-supplied classification ceiling SHALL be resolved against recorded clearance before it is bound, and the resolved value SHALL be the one enforced.

sentences.heading: Clearance and the effective ceiling
sentences.sentence: KF-SAS-RQ-038.** A clearance SHALL be organization-scoped and effective-dated, and the effective ceiling SHALL be the minimum of the clearance and any assignment ceiling.

sentences.heading: Access is a grant
sentences.sentence: KF-SAS-RQ-039.** Read authorization SHALL be the intersection of row-level visibility and live grant coverage, and a principal with no grant SHALL have an empty corpus.

sentences.heading: Access is a grant
sentences.sentence: KF-SAS-RQ-040.** Two live grants for the same principal, scope and capability SHALL NOT overlap in time.

sentences.heading: Access is a grant
sentences.sentence: KF-SAS-RQ-041.** The read path and the write path SHALL consult the same grant view.

sentences.heading: Explaining a denial
sentences.sentence: KF-SAS-RQ-042.** The system SHALL be able to explain any access decision as a path ending in the specific grant or exclusion that determined it.

sentences.heading: Institutional acts and the act capability
sentences.sentence: KF-SAS-RQ-043.** An institutional act SHALL require a live act grant reaching every target or the organization, checked after targets are locked.

sentences.heading: Institutional acts and the act capability
sentences.sentence: KF-SAS-RQ-044.** Which actions are institutional SHALL be declared in the ontology and carried into the database, not encoded in application control flow.

sentences.heading: Service actors
sentences.sentence: KF-SAS-RQ-045.** Scheduled and automated work SHALL act as a declared service actor through the same write path as a human, and SHALL NOT have a privileged path around it.

sentences.heading: Service actors
sentences.sentence: KF-SAS-RQ-046.** A service actor SHALL be refused every institutional act, regardless of the grants that reach it.

sentences.heading: Separation of duty
sentences.sentence: KF-SAS-RQ-047.** Where an act judges the product of another act, the system SHALL refuse it to the actor who performed the act being judged.

sentences.heading: Identity at the edge
sentences.sentence: KF-SAS-RQ-048.** Authentication SHALL establish only the subject, and every authorization question SHALL be answered from recorded state in the database.

sentences.heading: Identity at the edge
sentences.sentence: KF-SAS-RQ-049.** A deployment profile that permits fixed non-authoritative identity SHALL be distinct from every profile that serves records, and SHALL NOT be reachable from one by configuration.

sentences.heading: The dispatcher is the only write seam
sentences.sentence: KF-SAS-RQ-050.** All controlled writes SHALL pass through one dispatcher, in one transaction per act, and no other path SHALL be able to apply a controlled change.

sentences.heading: The action lifecycle
sentences.sentence: KF-SAS-RQ-051.** Authority SHALL be resolved before any state is materialized, and target coverage SHALL be asserted after targets are locked.

sentences.heading: Materializers and effects
sentences.sentence: KF-SAS-RQ-052.** Targets SHALL be locked in a canonical order, and an act SHALL refuse a target that is not visible under the bound access context.

sentences.heading: Materializers and effects
sentences.sentence: KF-SAS-RQ-053.** An act SHALL refuse a stale expected row version rather than applying a change over a read the caller did not make.

sentences.heading: Refusal codes
sentences.sentence: KF-SAS-RQ-054.** A refused act SHALL raise, and the result type SHALL NOT be able to represent a refusal.

sentences.heading: Idempotency and replay
sentences.sentence: KF-SAS-RQ-055.** A retried act SHALL apply at most once, and the replayed result SHALL be re-read from durable state rather than reconstructed.

sentences.heading: Idempotency and replay
sentences.sentence: KF-SAS-RQ-056.** The idempotency digest SHALL cover exactly the fields that determine mutation semantics, and SHALL exclude transport and read-scope fields.

sentences.heading: Idempotency and replay
sentences.sentence: KF-SAS-RQ-057.** A replay SHALL re-verify the integrity of the prior act's audit receipt before returning it.

sentences.heading: The audit chain
sentences.sentence: KF-SAS-RQ-058.** Every act SHALL append exactly one event to an append-only chain, computed by one implementation, in the same transaction as the act.

sentences.heading: The audit chain
sentences.sentence: KF-SAS-RQ-059.** The audit chain SHALL be independently verifiable from its recorded events without trusting the process that wrote them.

sentences.heading: The outbox
sentences.sentence: KF-SAS-RQ-060.** Side effects outside the act's transaction SHALL be driven from a durable record written inside it, and delivery SHALL be at-least-once rather than best-effort.

sentences.heading: Preflight and rehearsal
sentences.sentence: KF-SAS-RQ-061.** A rehearsal SHALL exercise the real write path inside a transaction that cannot commit, and SHALL NOT confer authority on any subsequent request.

sentences.heading: Bootstrap acts
sentences.sentence: KF-SAS-RQ-062.** Any act that cannot pass through the dispatcher SHALL still extend the audit chain using the same implementation, and SHALL be enumerable.

sentences.heading: The authority thesis, in SQL
sentences.sentence: KF-SAS-RQ-070.** The declared ontology SHALL be mirrored into the database such that an undeclared type, state or action token fails a referential constraint.

sentences.heading: Schemas as authority boundaries
sentences.sentence: KF-SAS-RQ-071.** Each schema SHALL name exactly one authority domain, and a derived schema SHALL be reconstructible from authoritative rows.

sentences.heading: Roles and DDL
sentences.sentence: KF-SAS-RQ-072.** Exactly one database role SHALL be permitted schema changes, and the application role SHALL NOT hold it.

sentences.heading: Row-level security
sentences.sentence: KF-SAS-RQ-073.** Row-level security SHALL be forced, not merely enabled, on every table holding governed records.

sentences.heading: Row-level security
sentences.sentence: KF-SAS-RQ-074.** A table brought under row-level security SHALL be declared in a form the boundary registry can discover statically.

sentences.heading: Policy predicates and plan shape
sentences.sentence: KF-SAS-RQ-075.** A policy predicate refactored for plan shape SHALL preserve visibility exactly, and SHALL run with invoker rights so that referenced tables continue to enforce their own policies.

sentences.heading: The JIT finding
sentences.sentence: KF-SAS-RQ-076.** Planner settings that a measurement showed to be load-bearing SHALL be applied identically in development, test and production, and a gate SHALL assert they agree.

sentences.heading: Triggers and immutability
sentences.sentence: KF-SAS-RQ-077.** A record asserting that an event occurred SHALL be immutable after it is written, except for fields that record subsequent verification of it.

sentences.heading: Check constraints and invariants
sentences.sentence: KF-SAS-RQ-078.** Every declared invariant SHALL be enforced by a database constraint or an action precondition, and the mapping from invariant to enforcement SHALL be asserted by a test.

sentences.heading: Migrations
sentences.sentence: KF-SAS-RQ-079.** Schema changes SHALL be ordered, forward-only in application, and applied from one declared sequence.

sentences.heading: Reversibility
sentences.sentence: KF-SAS-RQ-080.** A migration that cannot be reversed without loss SHALL be identified as such by a test, and SHALL NOT present a `down` path that appears safe.

sentences.heading: The registry mirror
sentences.sentence: KF-SAS-RQ-081.** A fresh installation SHALL verify that the seeded ontology matches the compiled source by digest, and SHALL refuse to proceed on a mismatch.

sentences.heading: Artifacts and versions
sentences.sentence: KF-SAS-RQ-090.** An artifact version SHALL be immutable once written, and a change to content SHALL produce a new version rather than modify an existing one.

sentences.heading: Digest addressing
sentences.sentence: KF-SAS-RQ-091.** Content SHALL be addressed by a digest over its exact bytes, and the producing toolchain's identity SHALL be recorded alongside the result.

sentences.heading: Ingestion: copy or reference, never by default
sentences.sentence: KF-SAS-RQ-092.** Ingestion SHALL require an explicit copy-or-reference intent, and SHALL refuse a batch that does not state one.

sentences.heading: Ingestion: copy or reference, never by default
sentences.sentence: KF-SAS-RQ-093.** The system SHALL support recording an external artifact by digest and locator without holding its bytes.

sentences.heading: Object storage and the working store
sentences.sentence: KF-SAS-RQ-094.** Object writes SHALL be create-only, and a failed act SHALL NOT leave unreferenced content in a store.

sentences.heading: Storage locations
sentences.sentence: KF-SAS-RQ-095.** A version's bytes MAY exist in several stores, each location carrying its own role and verification state.

sentences.heading: Storage locations
sentences.sentence: KF-SAS-RQ-096.** A read that falls back to a secondary copy SHALL serve only a copy whose digest has been verified.

sentences.heading: Replication and verification
sentences.sentence: KF-SAS-RQ-097.** Replication and verification SHALL be recorded acts, and a verification failure SHALL be recorded rather than retried into silence.

sentences.heading: Document parsing and atoms
sentences.sentence: KF-SAS-RQ-098.** A parse SHALL record the identity of the tool that produced it, including the executable version and not only its data-format version.

sentences.heading: Document parsing and atoms
sentences.sentence: KF-SAS-RQ-099.** A cross-host golden SHALL be frozen only over output that independent hosts were measured to agree on.

sentences.heading: Document parsing and atoms
sentences.sentence: KF-SAS-RQ-100.** Conversion loss SHALL be enumerated and recorded with the parse.

sentences.heading: Controlled documents
sentences.sentence: KF-SAS-RQ-101.** A controlled document's effective state SHALL change only through an institutional act, and a superseded revision SHALL remain retrievable.

sentences.heading: Compilation and rendering
sentences.sentence: KF-SAS-RQ-102.** Compilation SHALL be deterministic for a given source and toolchain, and the result SHALL be addressed by its digest.

sentences.heading: Preservation export
sentences.sentence: KF-SAS-RQ-103.** The preservation inventory SHALL be closed, and a governed table absent from it SHALL fail a gate rather than be silently omitted.

sentences.heading: The round trip
sentences.sentence: KF-SAS-RQ-104.** An export imported into an empty database SHALL re-export byte-identically.

sentences.heading: The round trip
sentences.sentence: KF-SAS-RQ-105.** Restore SHALL be exercised on a schedule using the shipped scripts, and its result SHALL be recorded.

sentences.heading: The master record
sentences.sentence: KF-SAS-RQ-110.** A person SHALL be able to obtain the complete set of records about them that they are authorized to see, as one compiled, sealed artifact.

sentences.heading: Corpus identity
sentences.sentence: KF-SAS-RQ-111.** A master record's identity SHALL be its corpus, and an unchanged corpus SHALL compile to the same record rather than a conflict.

sentences.heading: Corpus identity
sentences.sentence: KF-SAS-RQ-112.** Staleness SHALL be computed by comparing the current corpus to the recorded one, not asserted by the writer.

sentences.heading: Projections
sentences.sentence: KF-SAS-RQ-113.** Every reading of a corpus SHALL be a declared, versioned projection, and its members SHALL be a subset of the corpus.

sentences.heading: Projections
sentences.sentence: KF-SAS-RQ-114.** A projection's sections SHALL cover its corpus, with an explicit remainder, so that no member is silently omitted.

sentences.heading: Projections
sentences.sentence: KF-SAS-RQ-115.** Context assembled for an agent SHALL be a projection subject to the same invariants as a projection rendered for a person.

sentences.heading: The projection grammar
sentences.sentence: KF-SAS-RQ-116.** The projection grammar SHALL be closed and non-executable, and every definition SHALL be statically bounded in depth, size and runtime.

sentences.heading: Object Views
sentences.sentence: KF-SAS-RQ-117.** Every object type SHALL have a read view derived from ontology metadata, requiring no type-specific presentation code.

sentences.heading: The master-record boundary
sentences.sentence: KF-SAS-RQ-118.** Every governed table SHALL carry an explicit master-record boundary classification, and an unclassified table SHALL fail the build.

sentences.heading: The master-record boundary
sentences.sentence: KF-SAS-RQ-119.** No external system SHALL be resolved live into a master record; external content SHALL enter only as a governed row recording its digest.

sentences.heading: The withholding ledger
sentences.sentence: KF-SAS-RQ-120.** A compiled record SHALL enumerate what was withheld from it and on what basis.

sentences.heading: Search
sentences.sentence: KF-SAS-RQ-121.** Search SHALL use one index for all audiences, filtered at read time by the same authorization context as every other read.

sentences.heading: Search
sentences.sentence: KF-SAS-RQ-226.** A derived index SHALL NOT decide visibility from a denormalised copy of an authorization input; the decision SHALL be taken against the authoritative record in the same statement that reads the index.

sentences.heading: Identifier allocation
sentences.sentence: KF-SAS-RQ-130.** Identifier allocation SHALL be atomic with the act that requests it, SHALL skip occupied numbers rather than reissue them, and SHALL be refused for an undeclared namespace.

sentences.heading: Identifier allocation
sentences.sentence: KF-SAS-RQ-131.** An act SHALL be able to return a value it computed, read back from durable state, and a replay SHALL return the same value.

sentences.heading: Warrants
sentences.sentence: KF-SAS-RQ-132.** KF SHALL be the institutional authority for a federated record without becoming its Source Holder, and SHALL record the source system's computed digests rather than substituting its own.

sentences.heading: Warrants
sentences.sentence: KF-SAS-RQ-133.** A federated record's identity in KF SHALL be the identity the Source Holder uses.

sentences.heading: Publication
sentences.sentence: KF-SAS-RQ-134.** Publication SHALL write exactly one public copy, verified, and the database SHALL refuse a public copy written by any other act or into any non-public store.

sentences.heading: Publication
sentences.sentence: KF-SAS-RQ-135.** Unpublication SHALL be a recorded state change over the published copy, and SHALL NOT delete it.

sentences.heading: External source holders
sentences.sentence: KF-SAS-RQ-136.** External content admitted as a copy SHALL record the source system, the exact revision read, and the identity of any converter that produced the bytes held.

sentences.heading: External source holders
sentences.sentence: KF-SAS-RQ-137.** A conversion that cannot be performed at the cited revision SHALL be refused rather than performed at a different one under the cited label.

sentences.heading: Federation adapters
sentences.sentence: KF-SAS-RQ-138.** A federation adapter SHALL import governed metadata and a digest, and SHALL NOT create a writable local copy that could diverge from its authority.

sentences.heading: What KF refuses to be a second authority for
sentences.sentence: KF-SAS-RQ-139.** The product SHALL be separable from any one deployment's identifier registry, and where that separation does not yet hold, the specific coupling SHALL be recorded.

sentences.heading: What KF refuses to be a second authority for
sentences.sentence: KF-SAS-RQ-192.** The deploying organization's identity SHALL be configuration, and SHALL NOT be compiled into the product's source.

sentences.heading: The ML registry
sentences.sentence: KF-SAS-RQ-140.** Model lineage SHALL be append-only and SHALL record measurements and provenance without the underlying data.

sentences.heading: Secure objects
sentences.sentence: KF-SAS-RQ-141.** Access to a secure object SHALL be by an issued, recorded capability with a declared purpose.

sentences.heading: Work control
sentences.sentence: KF-SAS-RQ-142.** The full work-control path SHALL be reachable through declared actions alone, and an end-to-end test SHALL exercise it without direct table writes.

sentences.heading: Product configuration and quality
sentences.sentence: KF-SAS-RQ-143.** Product configuration, quality and engineering records SHALL be governed by the same object, act and audit model as every other record, with no privileged path.

sentences.heading: The HTTP surface
sentences.sentence: KF-SAS-RQ-150.** The HTTP layer SHALL hold no authority of its own, and SHALL make no refusal the write path does not.

sentences.heading: The command line
sentences.sentence: KF-SAS-RQ-151.** Operator commands SHALL accept secrets only by file reference, and SHALL refuse an inline secret by name.

sentences.heading: The schema pack
sentences.sentence: KF-SAS-RQ-152.** A release package SHALL carry its known gaps, and an approval SHALL commit to the gaps as well as to the content.

sentences.heading: The schema pack
sentences.sentence: KF-SAS-RQ-153.** A package manifest SHALL NOT contain its own digest, and verification of the manifest SHALL be a distinct act.

sentences.heading: R01 preservation
sentences.sentence: KF-SAS-RQ-154.** An approved definition SHALL be preserved byte-identically, every addition SHALL be declared by name, and every divergence SHALL be enumerated exhaustively with a rationale.

sentences.heading: The registry pack
sentences.sentence: KF-SAS-RQ-155.** A rule that cannot be machine-enforced SHALL be recorded as such rather than presented as enforced.

sentences.heading: Generated artifacts
sentences.sentence: KF-SAS-RQ-156.** Generated artifacts SHALL contain no non-deterministic content, and SHALL be verified by regeneration in continuous integration.

sentences.heading: The web boundary
sentences.sentence: KF-SAS-RQ-157.** The presentation layer SHALL contain no authority decision and no business rule.

sentences.heading: Versioning and compatibility
sentences.sentence: KF-SAS-RQ-158.** Every canonical format SHALL carry a version tag in its digest preimage, and a format change SHALL produce a new tag rather than reinterpret existing digests.

sentences.heading: The platform contract
sentences.sentence: KF-SAS-RQ-160.** The deployment SHALL target exactly one declared platform contract, and SHALL state it rather than implying portability.

sentences.heading: Host requirements
sentences.sentence: KF-SAS-RQ-161.** Every host requirement SHALL be stated and probed, and provisioning SHALL be exercised on a minimal image rather than on one whose defaults hide the dependency.

sentences.heading: Release and promotion
sentences.sentence: KF-SAS-RQ-162.** The artifact tested SHALL be the artifact deployed, promoted without rebuilding, and installation SHALL be atomic and reversible.

sentences.heading: Services and timers
sentences.sentence: KF-SAS-RQ-163.** Each service SHALL run under a distinct unprivileged account, sharing one only where two units require identical secrets and identical data.

sentences.heading: Services and timers
sentences.sentence: KF-SAS-RQ-164.** The alerting path SHALL be exercised on a schedule independently of any failure, and its delivery to a person SHALL be evidenced.

sentences.heading: Backup and restore
sentences.sentence: KF-SAS-RQ-165.** A backup SHALL be verified at its destination, and restore SHALL be proven on a schedule using the shipped procedure.

sentences.heading: Backup and restore
sentences.sentence: KF-SAS-RQ-166.** An archiving command SHALL fail on a write it did not perform, and SHALL NOT report success for a skipped file.

sentences.heading: Checkpoints
sentences.sentence: KF-SAS-RQ-167.** Audit checkpoint signing SHALL run in a process the serving application cannot reach the key of, and that isolation SHALL be evidenced on the host.

sentences.heading: Commissioning
sentences.sentence: KF-SAS-RQ-168.** Commissioning SHALL require evidence produced on the host being commissioned, and service availability SHALL NOT be accepted as evidence of authorisation.

sentences.heading: Commissioning
sentences.sentence: KF-SAS-RQ-169.** Controls that no automated check covers SHALL be enumerated as such.

sentences.heading: Threat model
sentences.sentence: KF-SAS-RQ-170.** Every documented control SHALL cite the artifact that proves it, and a gate SHALL verify that every cited path resolves.

sentences.heading: What operations cannot supply
sentences.sentence: KF-SAS-RQ-171.** Claims requiring host, provider or human evidence SHALL be marked as outstanding until that evidence exists, and SHALL NOT be inferred from a passing test.

sentences.heading: Governance of this specification
sentences.sentence: KF-SAS-RQ-180.** This specification SHALL be governed by digest, its accepted revisions SHALL be immutable, and acceptance SHALL be performed by a human actor.

sentences.heading: Governance of this specification
sentences.sentence: KF-SAS-RQ-181.** Every copy or export of this specification SHALL state the accepted revision and digest it reproduces.

sentences.heading: Decision records
sentences.sentence: KF-SAS-RQ-182.** Architectural decisions SHALL be recorded with their measurement and rejected options, and a superseded record SHALL be retained in full.

sentences.heading: The requirement ladder
sentences.sentence: KF-SAS-RQ-183.** Requirement identifiers SHALL be append-only, and requirement status SHALL be derived from evidence rather than recorded in this document.

sentences.heading: Known gaps and accepted limits
sentences.sentence: KF-SAS-RQ-184.** A requirement cited from another repository SHOULD be resolvable against this document by a tool, and until it is, such a citation SHALL be treated as an unverified claim.

sentences.heading: Known gaps and accepted limits
sentences.sentence: KF-SAS-RQ-186.** The set of tables forced under row-level security SHALL be derivable from the migrations, and any difference between that set and the running database SHALL be reconciled.

sentences.heading: Neighbouring programs
sentences.sentence: KF-SAS-RQ-185.** KF SHALL NOT duplicate the authority of a neighbouring program, and SHALL record which program owns each federated fact.
